chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fuddal, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu al-Hasan Zakariyya ibn Yahya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whatever of His Knowledge Allah has concealed from the servants is unburdened from them.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean when Allah conceals His knowledge from the servants?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the scope of human accountability by distinguishing between Divine Knowledge that is explicitly revealed and that which remains concealed. This principle establishes that humans are only responsible for what Allah has made manifest, thereby relieving them of the burden of knowing the unseen details of God's essence or decrees that He chose to keep hidden. This hadith serves as a foundational theological boundary in Shia thought, preventing excessive speculation about the divine while emphasizing obedience to revealed guidance.
